### Category Comparisons and Tradeoffs

#### 1. Scoring
* **Michael Jordan:** Averaged 30.1 points per game across 1,072 career regular-season games [T1, T5]. He earned 10 scoring titles [T3]. In terms of high-scoring regular-season games, he recorded 562 games with 30+ points, 173 games with 40+ points, and 31 games with 50+ points [T1]. Jordan also registered four seasons scoring over 30 points per 75 possessions at +6% relative true shooting (rTS) [jordan_defense_2720].
* **LeBron James:** Averaged 26.8 points per game across 1,622 career regular-season games [T2, T5]. He earned 1 scoring title [T4, lebron_accolades_320]. He recorded 577 games with 30+ points, 79 games with 40+ points, and 14 games with 50+ points [T2]. He produced one season scoring over 30 points per 75 possessions at +6% rTS [jordan_defense_2720].
* **Tradeoff:** Jordan provides a higher per-game scoring average (+3.3 PPG) [T5], nine more scoring titles [T3, T4], and a vastly higher frequency of 40-point (173 to 79) and 50-point (31 to 14) games [T1, T2]. LeBron holds a slight edge in total career games with 30+ points (577 to 562), achieved over a longer career [T1, T2].

---

#### 2. Defense
* **Michael Jordan:** Selected to 9 NBA All-Defensive First Teams and won 1 Defensive Player of the Year award (DPOY) [T3].
* **LeBron James:** Selected to 5 NBA All-Defensive First Teams and 1 All-Defensive Second Team [T4, lebron_accolades_320]. He has won 0 DPOY awards [T4].
* **Tradeoff:** Jordan holds the advantage in top-tier defensive honors with a Defensive Player of the Year trophy and 9 First Team selections compared to LeBron’s 5 First Team selections and zero DPOYs [T3, T4].

---

#### 3. Accolades
* **Michael Jordan:** 
  * Championships: 6 [T3]
  * Finals MVPs: 6 [T3]
  * Regular-Season MVPs: 5 [T3]
  * All-NBA Teams: 10 First Team, 1 Second Team, 0 Third Team (11 total) [T3]
* **LeBron James:** 
  * Championships: 4 [T4]
  * Finals MVPs: 4 [T4]
  * Regular-Season MVPs: 4 [T4, lebron_accolades_160]
  * All-NBA Teams: 13 First Team, 4 Second Team, 4 Third Team (21 total) [T4, lebron_accolades_160]
  * Additional Accolades: 1 Rookie of the Year award [lebron_accolades_320]
* **Tradeoff:** Jordan leads in the highest-level hardware—championships (6 to 4), Finals MVPs (6 to 4), and regular-season MVPs (5 to 4) [T3, T4]. LeBron leads in aggregate All-NBA selections (21 to 11), including more First Team honors (13 to 10) [T3, T4].

---

#### 4. Longevity
* **Michael Jordan:** Played 15 seasons and 1,072 career regular-season games [T1].
* **LeBron James:** Played 23 seasons and 1,622 career regular-season games [T2].
* **Tradeoff:** LeBron holds a substantial longevity advantage, playing 8 more seasons and 550 more regular-season games than Jordan [T1, T2], which enabled him to accumulate more total career All-NBA selections (21 vs. 11) [T3, T4] and 30+ point games (577 vs. 562) [T1, T2].

---

#### 5. Playoffs
* **Michael Jordan:** Won 6 championships and 6 Finals MVPs [T3], appearing in 179 playoff games [jordan_playoffs_2560]. In postseason play, Jordan maintained his scoring volume and creation with almost no loss in efficiency, helping Chicago achieve a relative playoff offensive rating improvement (+7) during the 1990s [jordan_defense_2720].
* **LeBron James:** Won 4 championships and 4 Finals MVPs [T4]. An eight-year playoff metric shows that LeBron’s Cavaliers–Heat teams topped Jordan’s Bulls [jordan_defense_4480].
* **Tradeoff:** Jordan achieved a greater total number of titles (6) and Finals MVPs (6) alongside remarkable scoring resiliency [T3, jordan_defense_2720]. LeBron achieved 4 titles and 4 Finals MVPs [T4], leading multi-year postseason runs whose metrics rivaled and surpassed Jordan's Chicago teams over an eight-year span [jordan_defense_4480].

---

### Separation of Factual Evidence from Subjective GOAT Judgments

* **Factual Evidence:**
  * Jordan has higher per-game scoring (30.1 vs. 26.8 PPG) [T5], more scoring titles (10 vs. 1) [T3, T4], more 40+ and 50+ point regular-season games [T1, T2], more championships (6 vs. 4) [T3, T4], more Finals MVPs (6 vs. 4) [T3, T4], more regular-season MVPs (5 vs. 4) [T3, T4], and more All-Defensive First Team selections (9 vs. 5) plus a DPOY [T3, T4].
  * LeBron has significantly greater career length (23 seasons vs. 15; 1,622 games vs. 1,072) [T1, T2], more total All-NBA selections (21 vs. 11) [T3, T4], more All-NBA First Team nods (13 vs. 10) [T3, T4], and more total 30-point games (577 vs. 562) [T1, T2].

* **Subjective GOAT Judgments:**
  * Choosing between the two depends on subjective weighting: prioritizing peak dominance, scoring volume efficiency, and championship conversion favors Jordan's case; prioritizing prolonged career durability, multi-decade elite All-NBA play, and cumulative contributions favors LeBron's case.
